newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends up on Tokyo, light buying.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends up on Tokyo, light buying.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices closed higher in tandem with a strong futures market in Tokyo, and light demand for the SMR10 and SMR20, traders said.
"The price is more or less an adjustment based on Tokyo," said a trader. "But there was some covering for the 10 and 20, so demand was there."
An official trade source reported a small volume of SMR10 sold to Beijing at 255 cents a kg for May shipment and another small consignment of SMR20 for Milan, done at 250 cents a kg for May.
At the close, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board quoted June RSS1 buyer at 271 cents ($1.08) a kg, up half cent from Monday. June SMR 20 buyer ended 1.50 cents up at 256 cents.
Trading houses offered the SMR CV at 328 cents, SMR L at 307 cents, SMR 5 at 266, SMR 10 at 258 and drum latex at 226 cents.
The INRO five-day average fell to 207.32 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on May 12, compared to 207.62 on May 9.
The daily indicator rose to 207.14 from 207.10 previously. -- K. Baranee (603-230-7510) ($1=2.5060 ringgit)
